planned_anchors.what_is_missing: QymCAD does report progress and trouble — through one status STRING and a problem report — which is the idea OM9 keeps: the run tells the program what happened. What is missing is structure and safety: there are no typed events, no order, no observer seam, and a listener that fails has no defined consequence for the run it is watching.

implemented_api_before_this_task: status_surface.rs owned the user-visible line and its bounded tail (OM9-L3-01-01-007), and transcript.rs owned the typed history
session.rs reported nothing structured: a run's steps were visible only through prompt() and the document
om9-core/src/transaction.rs has an internal observer concept for the coordinator, but nothing at the command level
gap_found_by_this_task: There was no typed event at all: no Started/Progress/Warn/Finished, no ordering, and no way for a listener to watch a run.

A failing listener had no defined consequence. notify() now contains a panicking observer with catch_unwind and returns whether the observer survived, so a broken listener cannot abort a dispatch or leave a transaction half-applied; notify_all() counts the survivors.

Added: command_events.rs (EventKind, EventOutcome, CommandEvent, EventLog with a total sequence and a bound of 256, Observer, notify, notify_all) and the session wiring that emits Started on dispatch, Progress on the first point of a two-point command, Finished(Committed|Cancelled|Refused) at the end, plus Controller::warn for a refusal inside a run.
reuse_decision: ADAPT the 'the run reports what happened' habit of gui.rs; ADD typed events, the total order and the contained observer seam.
